newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says HK flights to continue after handover.
newsitem.headline: Germany says HK flights to continue after handover.

text.p: Traffic rights for airlines between Germany and Hong Kong will not be endangered by the integration of the territory into China next year, the German transport ministry said on Wednesday.
The German cabinet has approved a bill to bring into law a provisional air accord made between Bonn and Hong Kong in May 1995, a ministry statement said.

German Transport Minister Matthias Wissman said: "The agreement contributes to the strengthening of the German economy since scheduled flights between Germany and Hong Kong, which were previously only granted on the basis of provisional rights, will be put onto a legal basis."

He added: "Concerning the integration of Hong Kong into China in the middle of next year, it has been ensured that the traffic rights granted to Germany will not be endangered after the provisional rights are put onto an internationally legally binding basis."
The air accord also allows for flights between Germany and the territory to be increased after the planned opening of Chep Lap Kok airport in 1998, the statement said.
The lack of space at the existing Kai Tak airport meant no additional flights were possible before then, it added.
At present, Cathay Pacific flies daily passenger services and five freighter services a week between Hong Kong and Frankfurt.
Deutsche Lufthansa also operates daily flights and five freighter services on the same route.
